title: Semidefinite Programming-Based Decoupling Capacitor Placement for Power Distribution Network Optimization
problem: Decoupling capacitor placement for power distribution networks is formulated as nonlinear optimization, causing traditional heuristics to converge to local minima or search unnecessarily.
motivation: Optimal decap placement minimizing count improves circuit reliability and board cost, critical for high-speed PCB design.
method: Decoupling capacitors smooth voltage delivery by storing energy in power distribution networks. Traditional optimization methods get stuck in local optima. This approach models the problem as integer semidefinite programming (SDP—a mathematical optimization framework), then relaxes integer constraints to enable efficient solving and reduces connection points (ports) to improve scalability. An adaptive optimization scheme further refines the result.
key_novelty: The core insight is reformulating the nonlinear decap placement problem as integer semidefinite programming, which enables deterministic global optimization instead of heuristic local search.
contributions: Nonlinear-to-integer-SDP problem reformulation for decap placement
Integer relaxation and port reduction techniques for scalability
Adaptive optimization scheme improving solution quality
Outperforms state-of-the-art heuristics and commercial tools in both quality and runtime

metrics.ppa: better solution quality than commercial tool

limitations: Evaluation on PCBs; applicability to on-chip PDN optimization not discussed.
